interpretation: Decisions apply to the assessed contributions, not every clause in an RG. Retained proofs are partial and conditional on their model assumptions.

groups.title: Validated configuration and component modification

It lacks actual named Inner/Outer/Gray-Firewall event-to-SIEM binding and configured analysis/alerts. Audit offload is not automatically SIEM. Do not count incidental AW clauses as SIEM coverage.

groups.title: Cross Domain Solution approval conditions
groups.reason: The stated claim requires official CDS approval and registration. A relay implementation or theorem cannot confer those statuses.
groups.action: Check the exact CDS and its authoritative approval records.
groups.boundary: Separate any independently specified technical CDS isolation property from the approval requirement.
groups.clause: All selected source clauses reviewed; no positive clause supported by the current setup and retained evidence.
groups.historical_contribution: Software CDS relay is unapproved. Required CDS approval/registration/authority records are absent; unselected branch would be vacuous.

groups.title: Physical protection, authorized access, and disposal
groups.reason: Facility access, classification of physical protection, and disposal are physical and organizational controls absent from the model.
groups.action: Use authorized physical inspections and lifecycle records.
groups.boundary: Software proofs can support particular technical mechanisms but cannot establish the stated physical controls from network snapshots.
groups.clause: All selected source clauses reviewed; no positive clause supported by the current setup and retained evidence.
groups.historical_contribution: Physical classified-facility protection/access and secure disposal evidence absent. Host UUID/container isolation does not prove those properties.

groups.title: Parallel Inner components and distinct Outer internal interfaces
groups.reason: The selected result supplies one firewall-compatible branch from each Inner to its Outer. Checking explicit paths or running graph reachability directly establishes that existence claim.
groups.action: Check the branch paths, parallel placement, distinct physical interfaces, and absence of prohibited trunking using the appropriate topology and hardware records.
groups.boundary: Reuse the existing path library when those paths are witnesses for a larger proof. Avoid a new parallel-placement theory merely to convert a finite path into reachability.
groups.clause: SR16 parallel-placement structural subset: each of eight shared Inners has a Gray path to its Outer without traversing another Inner.
groups.historical_contribution: SR16 parallel-placement structural subset: each of eight shared Inners has a Gray path to its Outer without traversing another Inner. Shared Gray may admit other walks. Physical NIC separation and complete hardware placement remain open.

groups.title: Interoperable components across communicating sites
groups.reason: The current result reuses a general argument that mixed encapsulation and encryption preserve the original Ethernet header. That argument can cover modeled executions beyond a successful probe.
groups.action: Keep the shared preservation theorem and use actual traces and traffic tests to validate concrete pairings.
groups.boundary: Ordinary vendor interoperability still needs testing. The useful formal claim concerns modeled payload/header preservation, not blanket product compatibility.
groups.clause: Peer interoperability: actual forward and reverse useful bridged MACsec/L2TP/ESP paths deliver restored opaque Ethernet headers.

groups.title: Firewall requirements when combining capability packages
groups.reason: The current setup has no selected companion CP with its applicable mandatory clauses. The immediate missing work is determining the combined requirements.
groups.action: Identify the other CP and its applicable firewall obligations, then inspect the selected configuration.
groups.boundary: Once selected, all-path firewall placement should reuse RG-013/RG-034's general proofs; it does not need an independent combined-CP graph theory.
groups.clause: All selected source clauses reviewed; no positive clause supported by the current setup and retained evidence.
groups.historical_contribution: Combined-Gray demonstration does not identify an actual selected other CP and its applicable mandatory firewall clauses. Unselected implication would be vacuous.

groups.title: Approved physical paths out of Red Networks
groups.reason: A single unprotected egress path can defeat the design. The useful structural claim covers every observed Red-to-outside path.
groups.action: Reuse the path-separation argument to require an Inner crossing, then connect that crossing to the protection proof when claiming encrypted egress.
groups.boundary: The current theorem covers virtual topology. Physical links and official approval of alternate protection remain external obligations.
groups.clause: SR14 structural egress protection: every observed virtual path from eight Red hosts to outside Red crosses an Inner.

groups.title: Operational security updates and TEMPEST policy
groups.reason: The claimed duties depend on an actual update process and external policy, including TEMPEST requirements. Version strings and fabricated update events cannot establish them.
groups.action: Audit patch testing, installation, required schedules, and the applicable physical-emissions policy.
groups.boundary: A verified rollout controller could prove a specified update-order invariant. Such a controller is outside the current evidence.
groups.clause: All selected source clauses reviewed; no positive clause supported by the current setup and retained evidence.
groups.historical_contribution: No actual security-patch test/install lifecycle, authority-selected update schedule or TEMPEST policy. Version strings alone are insufficient.

groups.title: Hardware inventory and available baseline configuration
groups.reason: The counted application shows that one successful response contains a selected configuration fragment. Direct response-to-source comparison establishes that observation.
groups.action: Audit hardware inventory completeness, retrieve the maintained baseline, and compare its contents and access permissions.
groups.boundary: A fragment readback does not establish the existence, maintenance, or completeness of the whole baseline.
groups.clause: GD26 selected configuration availability: an authenticated Auditor receives the saved diagnostic filter configuration fragment.
groups.historical_contribution: GD26 selected configuration availability: an authenticated Auditor receives the saved diagnostic filter configuration fragment. The fragment is not the whole maintained device baseline; organization, maintenance and all devices remain open.

groups.title: Procurement documentation excludes classified-protection purpose
groups.reason: Procurement-document content needs an authentic document set and review for prohibited disclosures. The central difficulty is document coverage and meaning.
groups.action: Review acquisition records and use text checks to assist the responsible reviewer.
groups.boundary: A theorem about absent words would not establish absence of the prohibited purpose expressed in other language.
groups.clause: All selected source clauses reviewed; no positive clause supported by the current setup and retained evidence.
groups.historical_contribution: No actual procurement or contracting requirement records.

groups.title: Annual and NSA-authorized compliance audits
groups.reason: Annual audits, cooperation, and AO review are actions by organizations. They require genuine audit and delivery records.
groups.action: Track audit dates, scope, cooperation evidence, and review outcomes.
groups.boundary: A deadline checker can assist compliance operations; an emulation proof cannot establish those actions.
groups.clause: All selected source clauses reviewed; no positive clause supported by the current setup and retained evidence.
groups.historical_contribution: No actual annual audit or NSA access/notification records; lab tests are not an annual compliance audit.

groups.title: Registration, approval, annual renewal, and version updates
groups.reason: Registration, renewal, and version-transition compliance require authority-issued records and a documented deadline interpretation.
groups.action: Check approvals, dates, applicable CP versions, and approved exceptions against the authoritative documents.
groups.boundary: A workflow program could have verified deadline logic, but that would not establish that registration or approval actually occurred.
groups.clause: All selected source clauses reviewed; no positive clause supported by the current setup and retained evidence.
groups.historical_contribution: No actual NSA registration/AO approval or approved risk acceptance.

groups.title: Audit retention, storage monitoring, backup, and continuity
groups.reason: The current proof covers a frozen copy's interval coverage and equality across one observed restart. A complete byte/range comparison and a restart test address that bounded observation directly.
groups.action: Check the copied content, continuity, retention settings, capacity records, and actual restart recovery. Audit the annual and quarterly duties separately.
groups.boundary: A storage protocol with modeled crashes and concurrent writes could merit formal verification. The current observation-based contribution does not justify a separate TDN storage theory.
groups.clause: GD15 technical copy coverage: every byte of a frozen audit source is copied through contiguous committed batches.
groups.historical_contribution: Existing checked contiguous audit export and restart persistence. No annual retention or quarterly review claim. Existing selected positive contribution meets the revised partial-proof threshold.

groups.title: Infrastructure authentication alternatives
groups.reason: The current setup lacks the relevant infrastructure authentication and entropy evidence. The password alternative cannot be established by merely measuring string length.
groups.action: Audit the random-password generation process or the selected authentication service, and test router/switch authentication.
groups.boundary: A shared session-admission theorem may help a modeled service. Randomness and 112-bit entropy require a justified generator model and implementation evidence.
groups.clause: All selected source clauses reviewed; no positive clause supported by the current setup and retained evidence.
groups.historical_contribution: Actual infrastructure-device authentication/password-generation entropy/domain-authentication records absent. Outer role-admin TLS service does not establish authentication for infrastructure routers/switches.

groups.title: Incident triggers, required report fields, and reporting deadline
groups.reason: Actual incident classification, notification, and receipt within a deadline require operational records and human decisions.
groups.action: Check authentic incident timelines, report fields, delivery receipts, and the stated exceptions.
groups.boundary: A verified reporting workflow can prove its own scheduling logic under delivery assumptions. It cannot establish actual human reporting from synthetic incident entries.
groups.clause: All selected source clauses reviewed; no positive clause supported by the current setup and retained evidence.
groups.historical_contribution: No actual reportable incident/JIMS/NSA delivery records; synthetic incident formats do not establish reporting.

groups.title: Separation of administrative and auditing personnel
groups.reason: Different roles or credentials do not establish different people. The required separation relies on an authenticated personnel-to-role mapping.
groups.action: Audit appointments and identity/account assignments; evaluate any actually selected mandatory-access policy.
groups.boundary: A formal role-conflict checker can be reused, but it cannot supply the personnel facts.
groups.clause: All selected source clauses reviewed; no positive clause supported by the current setup and retained evidence.
groups.historical_contribution: Certificate role map does not establish different actual people. Docker default AppArmor does not encode SecurityAdministrator/Auditor mandatory-access-control roles. No selected implemented RB11 policy evidence.

groups.title: Personnel training and physical tamper inspections
groups.reason: Training and physical inspections are real-world events. Their occurrence and adequacy are not network-state properties.
groups.action: Review training records, appointments, inspection records, and the applicable periodicity policy.
groups.boundary: Simple date and completeness checks can support the review.
groups.clause: All selected source clauses reviewed; no positive clause supported by the current setup and retained evidence.
groups.historical_contribution: No actual training, appointment or physical inspection records.

groups.title: Revocation or CAK destruction before disposal
groups.reason: The current record has revocation tests but no disposal event. A before-disposal requirement needs authentic linked lifecycle events.
groups.action: Check that revocation or CAK-destruction initiation precedes each actual disposal authorization.
groups.boundary: If a retirement controller technically prevents disposal before revocation initiation, its ordering property could merit proof. The human disposal process still needs evidence.
groups.clause: All selected source clauses reviewed; no positive clause supported by the current setup and retained evidence.
groups.historical_contribution: Revocation tests exist, but no actual device-disposal event and before-disposal credential-removal ordering. Do not relabel ordinary revocation as disposal.

groups.title: Security Administrator operational duties
groups.reason: The counted contribution reuses a successful configuration readback as evidence of administrator monitoring. It establishes a narrow response fact, not the administrator's continuing duties.
groups.action: Keep the readback test and audit the actual monitoring, update, incident, and maintenance activities.
groups.boundary: Use shared access-control proofs for the administration API. Do not introduce an operational-duty model to relabel a returned configuration fragment.
groups.clause: Security Administrator monitoring: actual role-authorized diagnostic configuration readback.
groups.historical_contribution: Security Administrator monitoring: actual role-authorized diagnostic configuration readback. Human appointment and comprehensive ongoing administrative duties remain open.

groups.title: Auditor review duties and access boundary
groups.reason: The counted application checks that eight previously read events remain an exact prefix after one observed rotation. A direct ordered-content comparison can establish that fact.
groups.action: Compare complete records before and after rotation and test authorization and failure handling. Audit human review duties separately.
groups.boundary: A verified concurrent logging implementation could justify general retention proofs. The current captured-run result should not drive a separate audit-rotation abstraction in the network core.
groups.clause: p054:u014.s001: the actual Auditor log-management operation preserves all eight independently retrieved earlier audit entries through rotation and later append-only activity.
groups.historical_contribution: The authenticated Auditor successfully rotates the actual ND_O_A1 service log. All eight earlier readback records are preserved as an exact prefix of the captured archives and active log. Complete canonical event objects, client responses, runtime role/source/listener identity and archive contents are checked. The reconstructed pre-rotation active file is explicitly distinguished from the earlier independent readback. Human review, incident reporting, full component access restrictions and all future audit duties remain open.

groups.title: Optional Integrator involvement and duty scope
groups.reason: Integrator engagement and personnel duties require an actual engagement and its applicable responsibilities. An unselected optional branch establishes no substantive requirement.
groups.action: Use contracts, appointments, deliverables, and relevant technical test results when an Integrator is engaged.
groups.boundary: Reuse technical proofs for the delivered network; do not create a separate theorem for the permission to hire an Integrator.
groups.clause: All selected source clauses reviewed; no positive clause supported by the current setup and retained evidence.
groups.historical_contribution: No actual Integrator engagement/credential/contract records; unselected optional Integrator is vacuous.

groups.title: AO authorization evidence and lifecycle control
groups.reason: AO authorization and lifecycle acceptance are authoritative acts. Their existence cannot be inferred from a network model.
groups.action: Review approvals, assessment delivery, change control, and actual compromise-response records.
groups.boundary: The technical propagation of revocation updates may later merit a distributed-state proof, but it is a distinct clause needing implementation evidence.
groups.clause: All selected source clauses reviewed; no positive clause supported by the current setup and retained evidence.
groups.historical_contribution: No actual approving-authority lifecycle/acceptance records.

groups.title: Whole-solution testing and preserved results
groups.reason: The counted proof establishes that each of 12 test IDs maps to a nonempty saved path. A manifest/file checker is the direct tool for completeness and retained content.
groups.action: Check that required tests were run, their files exist, hashes match, results are reviewed, and the report was delivered as required.
groups.boundary: Keep tests as validation of model/implementation correspondence. A path-existence theorem does not establish test coverage or correctness.
groups.clause: Selected test-result retention: all 12 declared native management network probe results have retained raw records.
groups.historical_contribution: Selected test-result retention: all 12 declared native management network probe results have retained raw records. Testing Annex equivalence, complete test planning and authority submission remain open.

groups.title: Objective software and firmware signing algorithms
groups.reason: The signed demonstration utility is not bound to deployed Solution Component software. The useful first task is obtaining the actual artifacts and signature-verification evidence.
groups.action: Check component identity, signature algorithms, parameters, trust roots, and positive/negative verification results.
groups.boundary: A secure-update admission proof could be valuable if it models the actual component loader and relevant bypasses. The current demonstration does not support it.
groups.clause: All selected source clauses reviewed; no positive clause supported by the current setup and retained evidence.
groups.historical_contribution: ML-DSA87 demonstration signs a Twinet deployment utility outside Solution Component software inventory. No selected Firewall/VPN/AS executable/firmware is bound to that signed artifact. Existing theorem remains a diagnostic/example, not counted positive RG coverage.

groups.title: Redundant component and load-balancing permission
groups.reason: Additional redundant paths can introduce a firewall bypass. The selected deployment is a useful second application of the same all-path separation theorem.
groups.action: Reuse RG-034's graph theorem for the redundant topology and check each added component's conditions.
groups.boundary: Avoid inventing a separate redundancy theory for the same cut property. Failover correctness or availability would require additional behavioral evidence and claims.
groups.clause: Redundant components retain applicable CP placement: four actual redundant Outers have mandatory firewall-separated paths to selected Black transport.

groups.title: Optional additional controls and screening-router scope
groups.reason: The source permits the described additions without imposing a countable security obligation on them. A theorem should not be manufactured from that permission.
groups.action: Record architectural scope and any independently applicable requirements.
groups.boundary: If an added router changes paths, include it in the topology used by the existing safety proofs.
groups.clause: p022:u007.s001–s002 and p026:u010.s001–s006 are optional design/context and boundary classification. No source-faithful positive security obligation has been identified for counting.
groups.historical_contribution: The selected p022:u007 text explicitly places no configuration or security requirements on the added components. The p026:u010 screening-router text permits placement and classifies the router as part of Black, outside MSC. The existing concrete placement theorem is useful architectural accounting, but it does not discharge a security requirement clause under the revised counting rule.

groups.title: CP user legal undertaking and disclaimer
groups.reason: Legal undertaking and acceptance are outside the network model and require responsible legal/organizational review.
groups.action: Retain the document requirement and appropriate acceptance records.
groups.boundary: No network theorem establishes legal acceptance or enforceability.
groups.clause: All selected source clauses reviewed; no positive clause supported by the current setup and retained evidence.
groups.historical_contribution: No actual party acceptance of legal terms; document text alone cannot establish acceptance.
